title: Arithmetic models of a smooth group with a fibrewise nonempty open
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], $G\to S$ a smooth separated group algebraic space of finite presentation with integral geometric fibres, and $V\subseteq G$ a quasi-compact open subspace meeting every geometric fibre. For algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation also requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and separatedness means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. A group algebraic space is an algebraic space with multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over its base satisfying the group identities, without a commutativity assumption. A geometric fibre is the base change to an algebraically closed field at a point of the base; integral means reduced, irreducible and nonempty. For every $s\in S$ there exist an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$, an affine scheme $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a morphism $U\to T$, with $T$ Noetherian of finite Krull dimension, an integer $d\geq0$, a smooth separated group algebraic space $G_0\to T$ of finite presentation, and a quasi-compact open $V_0\subseteq G_0$, such that every geometric fibre of $G_0\to T$ is integral of dimension $d$ and meets $V_0$. There is an isomorphism of group algebraic spaces $G|_U\cong G_0\times_TU$ identifying $V\times_SU$ with $V_0\times_TU$. The dimension of each geometric fibre is its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: reduction to a base essentially of finite type over Z, made precise for the group and its open. Supporting descent: Stacks spaces-limits.tex Tags 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0CN2 (lemma-descend-smooth), 0851 (lemma-descend-separated-morphism), 07SN (lemma-descend-surjective). The geometric-integrality and constant-dimension clauses are part of the model assertion, not consequences asserted of 07SK alone. Local Deligne PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing it. The inclusion $U\to S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local], its pullback to the quasi-compact space $V$ is quasi-compact, so $V_U$ is quasi-compact. Smoothness persists by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. Finite presentation and separatedness of $G_U\to U$ persist by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], write $U=\varprojlim_iT_i$ with $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the finitely generated integer subalgebras of $A$. These form a small nonempty directed set (finite subsets of the set $A$ suffice). Their spectra are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Tag 07SK, setup for approximation; properties.tex Tag 01OX for the restricted open

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] to obtain a finitely presented model $H_i\to T_i$ of $G_U$. Its square and cube are finitely presented by base change and composition [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Descend $m:G_U^2\to G_U$, $\iota:G_U\to G_U$ and $e:U\to G_U$ by the morphism clause of the same limit-category node, using the square model for $m$ and the terminal object for $e$. The equations $m(m\times1)=m(1\times m)$ on the cube, $m(e,1)=1=m(1,e)$ on $H$, and $m(\iota,1)\Delta=e p=m(1,\iota)\Delta$ on $H$ hold over $U$. The equality clause makes these finitely many equations hold at a common later stage. Hence $H_i$ is a group and the given identification over $U$ is a group isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07SK, object/morphism/equality clauses applied to the finite group diagram

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-eventually-smooth, lem-sfb-space-descend-separated], increase $i$ so $H_i\to T_i$ is smooth and separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent] to the two-member cover $(G_U,V_U)$ of $G_U$, viewed as the limit of the qcqs spaces $H_j$: a compatible family over $H_i$ is exactly a map to $H_i$ together with a map to $U=\varprojlim T_j$, by the fibre-product universal property. It gives a quasi-compact open $W_i\subset H_i$ whose pullback is $V_U$. Here the transition maps of the $H_j$ are affine, as base changes of the affine maps $T_j\to T_i$, and [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source] gives qcqs sources. The map $W_i\to T_i$ is locally of finite presentation: it is the restriction of the smooth map $H_i\to T_i$ to an open. Its pullback $V_U\to U$ is surjective by the fibrewise nonemptiness hypothesis. Thus [lem-sfb-space-eventually-surjective-map] makes $W_i\to T_i$ surjective after increasing $i$ once more. All preceding properties persist at later stages by the cited statements.

source.place: Tags 0CN2, 0851, 0827 and 07SN; open restriction uses the chart definition of local finite presentation

proof.text: The scheme $T_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-integral-fibre-locus] to $H_i\to T_i$ and let $E\subset|T_i|$ be its constructible integral-fibre locus. Its inverse image in $U$ is all of $U$, since $G_U$ has integral geometric fibres and that node gives exact base-change equality. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible], the image of $T_j\to T_i$ lies in $E$ at all sufficiently late stages. Apply the same base-change equality again to conclude that every geometric fibre of $H_j$ is integral. Replace $i$ by such a $j$; the group operations and $W_i$ are pulled back with it.

source.place: Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible), applied to the smooth-space integral-fibre locus; no openness of that locus is claimed

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-fibre-dimension], $t\mapsto\dim(H_i)_{\bar t}$ is locally constant. Write $t_i$ for the image of $s$ and $d$ for its value. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood $T=D(a)\subset T_i$ of $t_i$ contained in the locus with value $d$. The inverse image of $D(a)$ in the affine $U$ is a principal affine open $U'$ containing $s$. Put $G_0=H_i\times_{T_i}T$ and $V_0=W_i\times_{T_i}T$. Restriction preserves the group identities, smoothness, separatedness, finite presentation, integral geometric fibres and surjectivity of the open; the group identities are pulled-back equations; smoothness and surjectivity of $V_0\to T$ persist by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality], finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] and separatedness by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]; integrality of the geometric fibres follows from Step 4 by the base-change equality of [lem-sfb-smooth-space-integral-fibre-locus], and the dimension assertion from the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-fibre-dimension]. A point of $V_0$ over $t$ gives a nonempty $(V_0)_{\bar t}$, so $V_0$ meets every geometric fibre. The map $W_i\to T_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], and so is its base change by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local]; since $T$ is affine this proves that $V_0$ is quasi-compact. The pullback isomorphism on $U'$ identifies its open with $V\times_SU'$.

source.place: Tag 02G1 and identity/translation dimension consequence; principal-open restriction of the model

proof.text: The coordinate ring of $T$ is $(A_i)_a$, still a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra: adjoin one variable $z$ and the relation $az=1$. It follows that $T$ is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The latter has a finite Noetherian affine cover and dimension one, since its prime ideals are $(0)$ and $(p)$ for prime integers $p$. Apply [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to obtain that $T$ is Noetherian of finite Krull dimension. Rename $U'$ as $U$. The data constructed in Steps 2--5 now satisfy every asserted clause. If $S$ is empty there is no point $s$ to treat.
